public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 126

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/126](https://www.erdosproblems.com/126)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter

namespace Erdos126

def IsMaximalAddFactorsCard (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := ∀ n,
    IsGreatest
      { m | ∀ (A : Finset ℕ), A.card = n →
        m ≤ (∏ ⟨a, b⟩ ∈ A.offDiag, (a + b)).primeFactors.card}
      (f n)

/--
Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that if $A\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ has $|A| = n$ then
$\prod_{a\neq b\in A}(a + b)$ has at least $f(n)$ distinct prime factors.
Is it true that $\frac{f(n)}{\log n} \to\infty$?

The answer is yes, and a machine-checked proof is available.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/tadamcz/erdos126/blob/2516785fe6bbc43e979cf6029c976d9f998a7fba/Erdos126/Resolutions/Erdos126_132usd_25h.lean#L3053"]
theorem erdos_126 : answer(True) ↔ ∀ (f : ℕ → ℕ), IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f →
    Tendsto (fun n => f n / Real.log n) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős and Turán proved [ErTu34] in their first joint paper that
$$
  \log n \ll f(n) \ll \frac{n}{\log n}
$$

[ErTu34] Erdős, Paul and Turan, Paul, _On a Problem in the Elementary Theory of Numbers_. Amer. Math. Monthly (1934), 608-611.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_126.variants.IsBigO
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f) :
    ((fun (n : ℕ) => Real.log n) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) ∧
      (fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun (n : ℕ) => n / Real.log n := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős says that $f(n) = o(\frac{n}{\log n})$ has never been proved.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_126.variants.isLittleO
    (f : ℕ → ℕ)
    (hf : IsMaximalAddFactorsCard f) :
    (fun (n : ℕ) => (f n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun (n : ℕ) => n / Real.log n) := by
  sorry

end Erdos126

reformulations.difference: Lean permits zero in A, whereas Erdős–Turán's original paper uses positive integers. This can change individual extremal values: the Lean function has f(2) = 0, witnessed by {0,1}, while the positive-integer minimum is 1. Nevertheless, all three declarations using this definition are equivalent to their positive-integer versions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write F₀ for the minimum over nonnegative integer sets and F₊ for the minimum over positive integer sets. For n ≥ 1, F₊(n−1) ≤ F₀(n) ≤ F₊(n): positive sets are admissible nonnegative sets, and any n-element nonnegative set contains a positive (n−1)-element subset whose sum-prime support is contained in the original support. In particular F₊(n) ≤ F₀(n+1). Since log(n+1)/log n → 1 and ((n+1)/log(n+1))/(n/log n) → 1, these inequalities transfer both directions of the divergence claim, both big-O bounds, and the little-o bound. Thus the finite-value difference changes none of the mathematical claims in the file.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. Scratch Lean proofs establish existence and uniqueness of the extremal function, positivity of every off-diagonal product, f(0)=f(1)=f(2)=0, and equivalence of the definition with one using unordered pairs. Thus neither the maximality hypothesis nor primeFactors' zero convention introduces vacuity. The printed statements confirm real division and the intended asymptotic directions; logarithm/division defaults at 0 and 1 are irrelevant atTop. The cited external proof has the same definition and conclusion. After small Lean/Mathlib compatibility adjustments in /workspace/review only, it compiled and its final theorem depended solely on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The source's current statuses agree with all three category tags.
